q: The study of fluids at rest is called _____.
e: The study of fluids at rest is called hydrostatics, while the study of fluids in motion is hydrodynamic.

q: The study of fluids at motion is called _____.
e: Hydrodynamic is the study of fluids at motion, whereas hydrostatics is the study of fluids at rest.

q: Pressure is defined as the force exerted normally on _____.
e: Pressure is defined as the force exerted normally on unit area, expressed as $p = \frac{F}{A}$.

q: In SI units, pressure is measured in _____.
e: In SI units, pressure is measured in 'pascal' (Pa).

q: The relation between pascal, newton and metre is $1 \text{ Pa} =$ _____.
e: One pascal is equivalent to one newton per square metre ($1 \text{ Pa} = 1 \text{ N m}^{-2}$).

q: The force in the pressure formula must be _____ to the surface.
e: The force in the pressure formula must be normal ($90^{\circ}$) to the surface.
Pressure is a scalar quantity because it has magnitude but no specific direction.

q: Pointed nails penetrate the surfaces because for a definite force, the exerted area is too _____.
e: For a definite force, a smaller exerted area results in higher pressure, allowing pointed nails to penetrate surfaces.

q: Sharp knives can cut more easily than blunt knives because of _____ cutting area.
e: Sharp knives have a smaller cutting area, which increases the pressure exerted for the same force.

q: Elephants have four large flat feet so they _____ the pressure and are less likely to sink into the ground.
e: Large flat feet increase the area, which reduces the pressure exerted on the ground.

q: In the FPS system, the unit of pressure is _____.
e: In the FPS system, the unit of pressure is pound per square inch (psi).

q: In Meteorology, the unit of pressure is _____.
e: In Meteorology, the unit of pressure is commonly expressed as hectopascal (hPa).

q: Standard Atmospheric Pressure is _____ atmosphere (1 atm).
e: Standard Atmospheric Pressure is defined as 1 atmosphere (1 atm).

q: The relation $1 \text{ atm} = 1.013 \times 10^5 \text{ Pa} =$ _____ millimetre mercury.
e: Standard atmospheric pressure is equivalent to 760 millimetre mercury (760 mm Hg).
One atmosphere is equal to 1013 hPa, which is also equal to 1013 millibar (mb).
One hectopascal is equal to 100 pascals and exactly 1 millibar (mb).
One pound per square inch (psi) is equivalent to $6.90 \times 10^3$ Pa.
